evidence.claim: Twitter sought judicial review of Indian government content-removal orders that included accounts supportive of an independent Sikh state, posts about farmer protests, and tweets critical of the government's COVID-19 handling.
evidence.title: Twitter pursues review of Indian orders to take down content
evidence.excerpt: Twitter sought judicial review of Indian government content-removal orders that included accounts supportive of an independent Sikh state, posts about farmer protests, and tweets critical of the government's COVID-19 handling.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a live legal challenge with specific content categories and the government's takedown demands.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Indian authorities under Modi's government, though the article does not prove personal direction by Modi.
contrary_evidence: The report describes a legal dispute, so the government's legal justification is not adjudicated here.

evidence.claim: India carried out at least 84 internet shutdowns in 2022, including at least 49 in Jammu and Kashmir, and the report says shutdowns were used during protests and other high-salience periods to assert control.
evidence.title: Five years in a row: India is 2022’s biggest internet shutdowns offender
evidence.excerpt: India carried out at least 84 internet shutdowns in 2022, including at least 49 in Jammu and Kashmir, and the report says shutdowns were used during protests and other high-salience periods to assert control.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Access Now is the leading shutdown-tracking NGO; the report is retrospective but directly covers 2022 and gives quantified country totals.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but squarely about 2022 shutdown practice.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shared attribution across central and state authorities; not all shutdowns are personally traceable to Modi.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes transparency and accountability gaps in how shutdown orders are documented, which limits precise central attribution.

evidence.claim: HRW said Indian authorities intensified and broadened the crackdown on activist groups and the media in 2022 and used abusive and discriminatory policies to repress Muslims and other minorities.
evidence.title: India: Suppression of Free Speech, Minorities
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Indian authorities intensified and broadened the crackdown on activist groups and the media in 2022 and used abusive and discriminatory policies to repress Muslims and other minorities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: High-quality annual rights reporting with a clear 2022 focus and direct statements about the BJP-led government.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on 2022 but explicitly centered on that year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to the BJP-led government under Modi, though the report aggregates central, state, and local conduct.
contrary_evidence: This is an annual overview, not a case-by-case judicial finding.

evidence.claim: RSF said Indian authorities escalated retaliatory measures against foreign correspondents by denying access or permits, including a September 2022 refusal affecting Vanessa Dougnac's right to work.
evidence.title: Foreign correspondents increasingly refused permits, visas, access in India
evidence.excerpt: RSF said Indian authorities escalated retaliatory measures against foreign correspondents by denying access or permits, including a September 2022 refusal affecting Vanessa Dougnac's right to work.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: RSF is a specialized press-freedom monitor and the page gives a concrete 2022 case plus broader pattern language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directed at the Indian administration under Modi, though the specific permit decisions are bureaucratic and not individually traced to him.
contrary_evidence: One named case does not quantify the full scale of the pressure on all foreign correspondents.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said laws amended in India threatened freedom of expression and peaceful assembly and discriminated against Muslims and LGBTI people, while also raising concerns about religious violence and arbitrary deprivation of nationality.
evidence.title: India: Persecution of minorities and shrinking space for dissent: Amnesty International: Submission to the 41st session of the UPR Working Group, November 2022
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said laws amended in India threatened freedom of expression and peaceful assembly and discriminated against Muslims and LGBTI people, while also raising concerns about religious violence and arbitrary deprivation of nationality.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed country submission for the 2022 UPR cycle, with explicit rights claims and period fit.
evidence.period_fit: Prepared for the 2022 UPR and describing the Modi period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Modi-era legal and policy environment, though not every measure began in 2022.
contrary_evidence: It is an advocacy submission, not an adjudicated finding.

evidence.claim: USCIRF said the Indian government promoted Hindu nationalism and facilitated systematic, ongoing, egregious violations of religious freedom, making the environment hostile to many non-Hindu communities.
evidence.title: Anti-Conversion Laws and Growing Intolerance in India
evidence.publisher: United States Commission on International Religious Freedom
evidence.excerpt: USCIRF said the Indian government promoted Hindu nationalism and facilitated systematic, ongoing, egregious violations of religious freedom, making the environment hostile to many non-Hindu communities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: USCIRF is a U.S. government commission; the statement is policy-oriented but directly tied to the Indian government's conduct.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 source about the Modi period and the religious-freedom environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly directed at the Indian government under Modi, though it is a broader rights assessment rather than a case finding.
contrary_evidence: This is an evaluative commission statement, not a judicial determination of individual incidents.

evidence.claim: The report says police publicly flogged four Muslim men in Gujarat and that the Madhya Pradesh government bulldozed Muslim-owned homes and shops after communal violence, with UN rapporteurs calling the demolitions punitive.
evidence.title: 2022 Report on International Religious Freedom: India
evidence.excerpt: The report says police publicly flogged four Muslim men in Gujarat and that the Madhya Pradesh government bulldozed Muslim-owned homes and shops after communal violence, with UN rapporteurs calling the demolitions punitive.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official U.S. government report summarizing documented 2022 incidents and citing UN rapporteurs and media corroboration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Primarily state and local attribution, with indirect responsibility at the Modi-led federal level through the political environment and tolerance of allied actors.
contrary_evidence: Much of the conduct is at state or local level, so federal command is indirect rather than proven.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that BJP leaders told officials to be extremely cautious about religion on public platforms after derogatory remarks about the Prophet Mohammed drew protests from Islamic nations.
evidence.title: India's ruling party asks officials to exercise caution on religious issues after Islamic nations protest
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that BJP leaders told officials to be extremely cautious about religion on public platforms after derogatory remarks about the Prophet Mohammed drew protests from Islamic nations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting, but accessed via a syndication host and only available here as a search snippet in this session.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to a communal-political crisis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the ruling party environment under Modi, though not to Modi's personal words.
contrary_evidence: The warning followed inflammatory remarks and unrest, so it is damage control rather than evidence of prior restraint.
